clue.text: Initially the winner

definitions.meaning: at the very start, before anything else happens
the one who comes first in a race is placed at the top

explanation.surface: A remark that the person who started ahead ended up winning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'to begin with' and, read literally, the position held by a race's victor.

clue.text: Perceptible percipience

definitions.meaning: able to be seen, read as a two-word phrase 'in view'
keen understanding or discernment

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it means visible; as one word it means penetrating understanding, a synonym of percipience.

clue.text: One American author-or two

definitions.meaning: Mark ..., the pen name of Samuel Clemens
an old word for a pair

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether one American writer or a pair is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain wrote Tom Sawyer; twain is also archaic for a pair, the number after one.

clue.text: Declared former spouse made demands

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
pressed means urged or insisted

explanation.surface: An announcement that a former husband or wife has been making demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To have expressed a view is to have stated or put it into words.

clue.text: Attacks commercials for Japanese pill bottles

parts.note: an inro is a small Japanese box worn at the belt to hold medicines
ads are advertisements

explanation.surface: Attacks on adverts promoting Japanese medicine containers.
explanation.walkthrough: An INRO is a traditional Japanese lacquered case for pills hung from a sash; 'for' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances made into enemy territory, raids or incursions.

clue.text: Come into one's inheritance and prosper

definitions.meaning: to follow an heir's predecessor in title or property
to do well, to thrive

explanation.surface: An heir comes into money and does well out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone in office or estate is one sense; the other is to achieve one's aims.

clue.text: What the snooper did from utter arrogance

indicators.note: utter as a verb means speak, so the word for arrogance is said out loud

parts.note: pride is haughtiness or conceit

explanation.surface: A snooper acted out of sheer arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like the adjective 'complete' but is the verb 'say', signalling a homophone of PRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooper nosed into others' business, peering inquisitively.

clue.text: Back State that's ringing and asking for aid

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for the state is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
pealing is the sound of bells ringing

explanation.surface: Someone supports a state that is calling out for help.
explanation.definitionFit: An appealing person is making an earnest request or plea for help.

clue.text: To make money in France is no joke

parts.note: to earn is to gain income from work
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: Making money in France is a serious business.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and sincere rather than jesting.

clue.text: Just the fish for a photographer

definitions.meaning: a food fish of warm seas
informal term for someone taking pictures, especially a press cameraman

explanation.surface: A fish described as ideal for someone taking pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a sea fish and, informally, a person who takes snapshots.

clue.text: Cheerful French frier

definitions.meaning: lively and bright in mood
a device or person that fries chips, which Americans call French fries

explanation.surface: A jolly Frenchman who fries things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like a nationality, but French fries are chips, so a French frier makes chips.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means bright and lively, and also a chip-shop or chip-frying machine.

clue.text: Doughboy mixed general a drink

parts.note: a doughboy is an American infantryman, a GI

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of the word general are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An American soldier mixes a cocktail for his general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doughboy' sounds like a baker, but it is old slang for a US soldier, GI; 'mixed' rearranges GENERAL into NGERALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with the root spice, often used as a mixer.

clue.text: Noted roué who sailed around the world

parts.note: read as 'note D': D is a musical note placed first
a rake is a dissolute man, a roué

explanation.surface: A famous libertine who circumnavigated the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' reads as famous, but it gives a note, D, put before the rake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seaman who circumnavigated the globe in the Golden Hind.

clue.text: Key office workers

parts.note: reads as essential staff, but means people who press keys all day in an office

explanation.definitionFit: Clerical staff who type press keyboard keys for a living.

clue.text: Performed to the end, although exhausted

definitions.meaning: acted or played a scene through to its finish
worn out, used up

explanation.surface: Actors finished the show though they were worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both completed in performance and, as an adjective, tired out or spent.

clue.text: Baby's father first supported nihilistic art movement

definitions.note: a noun phrase sense: one who backed the movement

parts.note: dada is a baby's word for father
first written as 1st, the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An infant's dad was the first to back an anarchic art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'one who supported': a follower of Dada, the anti-art movement of around 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Dada, the early twentieth-century anti-art movement that rejected convention and reason.

clue.text: Roundabout way to find amusement

definitions.meaning: a detour that takes traffic around a blockage
an entertainment or pastime

explanation.surface: A detour turns out to be fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a detour for traffic and also a pleasant pastime or distraction.

clue.text: One who gets on with the landlady

definitions.text: One who gets on with the landlady

parts.words: One who gets on with the landlady
parts.note: reads as someone friendly with her, but means a lodger who lives and eats in her house

explanation.definitionFit: A lodger takes room and meals in a landlady's house.

clue.text: They could make graduate sick in the Channel Islands

definitions.text: They could make graduate sick in the Channel Islands

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder

indicators.note: in says one piece sits within the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Germs might make a graduate ill in the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British islands off the coast of Normandy, and the whole clue doubles as a description of what germs might do to a visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, some of which cause disease.

clue.text: Chivalrous tale unites Catholic and Anglican

parts.note: Roman as in Roman Catholic
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A story of knights brings together two branches of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval romance is a story of knightly adventure and courtly love.

clue.text: Artillerymen very old — and showing it!

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
aged means old

explanation.surface: Elderly gunners whose faces show their years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to being old: ravaged features show the wear of age.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravaged means badly damaged, as a face marked by time.

clue.text: Knock onomatopoeia

definitions.meaning: a rapping at the door
a word formed to imitate the sound it names

explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates a rapid series of knocks or raps on a door.

clue.text: Pete and Des differ most profoundly

indicators.note: differ says the letters of the two names come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Two men named Pete and Des disagree as deeply as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest is the superlative of deep, meaning to the greatest depth or intensity.

clue.text: Man dressed in headgear of poor quality

indicators.note: dressed in says one piece wears the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man in a hat that looks shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap goods are inferior, shoddy or low-grade.

clue.text: Some of Grandpa's sepia photos faded

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Old brown-tinted family photographs that have lost their colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'photos' in the definition, but photos are not faded: 'faded' alone defines, and 'photos' completes the hiding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé means out of date, past its prime, like something whose day has gone.

clue.text: Ordered comrade to get presidential escort

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of comrade and to are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A fellow is told to join the president's convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as commanded but signals the anagram of COMRADE and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of cars, typically accompanying a head of state.

clue.text: A model held up to aspiring fable writers?

definitions.text: A model held up to aspiring fable writers?

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means the word for model is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A great example set before would-be writers of fables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses POSE to ESOP in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is the archetypal author of moral animal tales.

clue.text: Contemplates reasoning with one's lad?

definitions.meaning: watches without taking part
a parent saying '...' to argue with a boy

explanation.surface: A parent thinks about having a word with their boy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means observes as a spectator, and split as 'look, son' it is a parent's appeal.

clue.text: Attempts to meet Lawrence in Italy

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in that country

parts.note: tries are efforts
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Efforts to meet Lawrence while in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: TE are the initials of T. E. Lawrence, known as Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a port city in north-east Italy on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Helping me to tint design, but getting mixed up

indicators.note: design as a verb means plan or arrange, so the letters before it are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone helps tint a design but the colours get muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges HELPING ME TO TINT into the answer; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in a state of flux, being blended or undecided, is said to be in a crucible.
